title: Speech Bubbles: Understanding Comics with Scott McCloud

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And this is Scott McLeod.
sentences.zh: 我是斯科特·麦克劳德。

sentences.en: My name is Scott McLeod.
sentences.zh: 我叫斯科特·麦克劳德。

sentences.en: I'm a cartoonist and author, and I've been making comics for a few decades now.
sentences.zh: 我是一名漫画家和作家，创作漫画已经有几十年了。

sentences.en: Probably best known for non-fiction comics, especially a book called Understanding Comics,
sentences.zh: 我可能最以纪实漫画闻名，特别是那本叫做《理解漫画》的书，

sentences.en: where I explain how comics work in comics form.
sentences.zh: 我在书里用漫画的形式解释了漫画是如何运作的。

sentences.en: But I've also done fiction work, and I have a lot of different interests.
sentences.zh: 但我也创作过虚构作品，而且我有许多不同的兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm very easily distracted.
sentences.zh: 我非常容易分心。

sentences.en: Scott's book, Understanding Comics, which is 25 years old this year,
sentences.zh: 斯科特的书《理解漫画》今年迎来了出版25周年，

sentences.en: is a seminal deconstruction of comics as an art form and mode of communication.
sentences.zh: 它是作为一门艺术形式和沟通媒介的漫画的开创性解构之作。

sentences.en: A little cartoon Scott jumps between panels of the 215-page book,
sentences.zh: 一个卡通小人斯科特穿梭在这本215页的书的各个分镜之间，

sentences.en: explaining how pictures and words in combination create a new language for telling stories and describing the world.
sentences.zh: 解释了图像与文字的结合如何创造了一种用于讲述故事和描述世界的新语言。

sentences.en: The book was the culmination of a bunch of ideas that had been swirling around Scott's head for years.
sentences.zh: 这本书是多年来在斯科特脑海中盘旋的各种想法的结晶。

sentences.en: Everybody knew, or they thought they knew, what comics were, and it was a very limiting idea.
sentences.zh: 每个人都自以为知道漫画是什么，而那是一种非常局限的观念。

sentences.en: And I see video games and other media dealing with the same problem today, maybe even podcasts,
sentences.zh: 我看到电子游戏和其他媒介今天也面临着同样的问题，也许播客也是如此，

sentences.en: is that people have had this idea that comics were just four-color, cheaply printed, cheaply made,
sentences.zh: 人们一直觉得漫画只是那种四色印刷的、廉价印刷的、廉价制作的、

sentences.en: comics about almost all superheroes or funny animals, that they were disposable entertainment,
sentences.zh: 几乎全都是关于超级英雄或搞笑动物的漫画，觉得它们只是一次性娱乐，

sentences.en: that neither the writing nor the art was anything that was going to last or be significant.
sentences.zh: 无论是文字还是艺术都谈不上能流传后世或有什么重大意义。

sentences.en: And even though I saw a lot of comics that, you know, conformed to that definition,
sentences.zh: 尽管我看到过很多漫画确实，你知道的，符合那种定义，

sentences.en: I mean, there were certainly plenty of bad comics out there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时市面上确实有大量糟糕的漫画。

sentences.en: To me, it was just an art form.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，它只是一种艺术形式。

sentences.en: It was an art form that was capable of so much more.
sentences.zh: 这是一种拥有无限可能的艺术形式。

sentences.en: And I felt like the first step was wiping the slate clean and trying to approach it from almost a clinical,
sentences.zh: 我觉得第一步是抹去过去的成见，尝试从一种几乎是客观的、

sentences.en: value-neutral sort of standpoint, where it's just like, well, what are the essential elements?
sentences.zh: 价值中立的角度来接近它，就像是，好吧，核心要素到底是什么？

sentences.en: And the essential elements of comics are just putting one picture after another and substituting space for time.
sentences.zh: 漫画的核心要素就是把一个画面接在另一个画面后面，用空间取代时间。

sentences.en: You're just saying that as you move from one space to the next, you're moving from one moment to the next.
sentences.zh: 你只是在说，当你从一个空间移动到下一个空间时，你正在从一个时刻移动到下一个时刻。

sentences.en: And that idea, to me, had just limitless applications.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这个想法有着无限的应用可能。

sentences.en: And it drew a boundary around a continent of possibilities that, as far as I was concerned, we'd only just begun to explore.
sentences.zh: 它为一片充满可能性的广阔天地画出了一条边界，就我而言，我们才刚刚开始探索。

sentences.en: When you wiped the slate clean and started with a new definition of comics, or at least, you know, a refined definition of comics,
sentences.zh: 当你抹去成见，用一种对漫画的新定义，或者至少是一个，你知道的，更精致的定义重新开始时，

sentences.en: can you rattle it off the top of your head what the definition was from the book?
sentences.zh: 你能脱口而出书中给出的定义是什么吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 噢，当然。

sentences.en: Because, you know, my mentor, Will Eisner, had used the term sequential art.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，我的导师威尔·艾斯纳曾用过“连续艺术”这个词。

sentences.en: And I said, you know, for the most part, most 90% of the time, you can just say sequential art.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道的，在绝大多数情况下，90%的时间里，你直接说连续艺术就行了。

sentences.en: People get it.
sentences.zh: 人们能理解。

sentences.en: But then right away, they'll say things like, well, what about animation?
sentences.zh: 但紧接着，他们就会说，比如，那动画呢？

sentences.en: That's sequential art.
sentences.zh: 那也是连续艺术。

sentences.en: So I had to come up with the longer definition that erased as many loopholes as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须想出一个更长的定义，尽可能地消除漏洞。

sentences.en: And what I came up with was juxtaposed pictorial in other images in deliberate sequence, which just for fun, I got to, you know, like really narrow it down.
sentences.zh: 我得出的定义是：并置的图画及其他图像序列，为了好玩，我得，你知道的，真正把它精确限定一下。

sentences.en: Just in case you didn't fully absorb that definition, it's juxtaposed pictorial in other images in deliberate sequence.
sentences.zh: 以防你没有完全消化这个定义，它就是：并置的图画及其他图像序列。

sentences.en: Some people thought that, you know, we had to stop calling them comics and start calling them juxtaposed pictorial in other images in deliberate sequence.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为，你知道的，我们必须停止叫它们漫画，而开始叫它们并置的图画及其他图像序列。

sentences.en: I said, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: You just, you do that once and then you go back to calling them comics.
sentences.zh: 你只需，你用一次这个词，然后就继续叫它们漫画。

sentences.en: People put a lot of value on labels.
sentences.zh: 人们对标签赋予了很高的价值。

sentences.en: And a lot of folks, you know, they get all up in arms that, oh, they're calling them graphic novels these days.
sentences.zh: 很多人，你知道的，他们一听说现在管它们叫图像小说，就会气急败坏。

sentences.en: They're putting on air.
sentences.zh: 觉得这是在摆架子。

sentences.en: So it's like, no, no, no, you can call it comics if you want.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比，不，不，不，你想叫它漫画完全可以。

sentences.en: I was just saying that, you know, comics, we need to allow the word to take on new meanings.
sentences.zh: 我只是在说，你知道的，漫画，我们需要允许这个词承载新的含义。

sentences.en: And every art form has different modes of dress, right?
sentences.zh: 每一种艺术形式都有不同的着装风格，对吧？

sentences.en: You can read about something in film comment and then you can go to the Academy of Motion Pictures to see the awards ceremony and then you can go out and see a movie the next day.
sentences.zh: 你可以先在《电影评论》上读到某部作品，然后去电影艺术与科学学院看颁奖典礼，第二天你还可以去看一场电影。

sentences.en: Now, you're using these different words as different ways of illuminating the different functions, the different styles, the different moods that come out of that art form.
sentences.zh: 现在，你使用这些不同的词语，作为阐明这种艺术形式所产生的不同功能、不同风格、不同情绪的不同方式。

sentences.en: But it's okay.
sentences.zh: 但没关系。

sentences.en: You can still call them movies.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以叫它们电影。

sentences.en: You can still call them comics.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以叫它们漫画。

sentences.en: What term do you like?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢哪个术语？

sentences.en: I like comics because actually I think it's fairly dry.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢漫画，因为实际上我觉得它相当枯燥。

sentences.en: I think that it's been a long time since people thought that all comics had to be funny.
sentences.zh: 我觉得人们认为所有漫画都必须搞笑的时代已经过去很久了。

sentences.en: When I was growing up, everybody assumed that all comics were muscle-bound guys in skin-tight suits beating the crap out of each other.
sentences.zh: 我成长的时候，大家都以为所有的漫画都是肌肉猛男穿着紧身衣互相暴揍。

sentences.en: So, you know, so we'd already lost the original meaning and that rendered it just this dry little bundle of sticks,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们早就失去了它最初的含义，这使得它变成了一个枯燥的小柴捆，

sentences.en: this little collection of phonemes that you could pretty much stuff any meaning into.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个你可以往里面塞进几乎任何含义的小小音素集合。

sentences.en: And also it's quick.
sentences.zh: 而且它很简短。

sentences.en: It's short, two syllables.
sentences.zh: 很短，两个音节。

sentences.en: So, if I were to pick up a comic book or, you know, turn to the comic section of the newspaper, are there certain things that you could teach me,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我拿起一本漫画书，或者，你知道的，翻到报纸的漫画版块，有没有什么特定规律你能教给我，

sentences.en: like how to decode comics in a certain way that, like, you could tell me, like, well, the artist is trying to do this when they do this.
sentences.zh: 比如教我如何以某种方式去解码漫画，就像你可以告诉我，嗯，艺术家在这样做的时候是想达到这个目的。

sentences.en: What are little take-home facts about decoding a comic?
sentences.zh: 关于解码漫画，有哪些可以现学现用的常识呢？

sentences.en: Well, the first thing are the universals.
sentences.zh: 好吧，第一件事就是普遍性。

sentences.en: That is, if you're looking at a comic strip or a comic book or a graphic novel, there are a few things everybody has to do.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你在看一幅漫画、一本漫画书或一本图像小说，有几件事情是所有人必须做的。

sentences.en: Whether they want to or not, these are the obligatory decisions that they all make.
sentences.zh: 不管他们愿意与否，这些都是他们所有人必须做出的强制性决定。

sentences.en: And one of the first decisions they make is choosing their moments.
sentences.zh: 他们做出的第一个决定之一就是选择他们的时刻。

sentences.en: No matter what, you're breaking the world into moments.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，你都要把这个世界切分成一个个时刻。

sentences.en: And it's a non-trivial problem, as an engineer would say.
sentences.zh: 用工程师的话说，这不是一个微不足道的问题。

sentences.en: I'm a son of an engineer.
sentences.zh: 我是个工程师的儿子。

sentences.en: And, you know, because if you think about it, any kind of narrative that you want to tell can be broken down in an infinite number of ways.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，因为如果你仔细想想，你想讲述的任何叙事都可以用无数种方式来拆解。

sentences.en: You know, I could do a 10,000-panel graphic novel of me taking a spoonful of cereal from a bowl, right, and just lifting it up to my mouth.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我可以画一个由一万格组成的图像小说，内容是我从碗里用勺子舀一勺麦片，对吧，然后把它举到嘴边。

sentences.en: If you want, I could just break it down by microseconds, by nanoseconds.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，我可以把它拆解到微秒级、纳秒级。

sentences.en: Or I could do you a two-panel sequence of the entire history of the universe, right?
sentences.zh: 或者我可以为你画一个由两格组成的序列，涵盖宇宙的整个历史，对吧？

sentences.en: Big bangs, heat death, you're done.
sentences.zh: 大爆炸，热寂，这就完了。

sentences.en: So, that means that you can slice it up any way you like.
sentences.zh: 所以，这意味着你可以按照你喜欢的任何方式去切分它。

sentences.en: And yet, if I asked you, hey, what did you do yesterday?
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我问你，嘿，你昨天做了什么？

sentences.en: There's a part of your mind that immediately leverages this tremendous neural horsepower to deciding what matters.
sentences.zh: 你脑海中的一部分会立即调动这种惊人的神经算力来决定什么才是重要的。

sentences.en: You know, we have these wonderful saliency filters that choose the moments quite naturally.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们拥有这些美妙显著性过滤器，能够非常自然地选择出那些时刻。

sentences.en: And most cartoonists choose them pretty naturally.
sentences.zh: 大多数漫画家选择时刻时都非常自然。

sentences.en: They know once they have a story to tell, they know what moments matter.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们有了要讲的故事，他们就知道哪些时刻是重要的。

sentences.en: But they have to make that decision, even if they're not making it consciously.
sentences.zh: 但他们必须做出那个决定，哪怕他们并非有意识地在做。

sentences.en: And then, from that point, you have to choose the angles, the framing.
sentences.zh: 然后，从那个点开始，你必须选择角度、构图。

sentences.en: How close are you going to get to that thing you want to show?
sentences.zh: 你打算离你想展示的东西有多近？

sentences.en: How far away are you going to be?
sentences.zh: 你打算离得多远？

sentences.en: What angle?
sentences.zh: 什么角度？

sentences.en: Is it going to be worm's eye view, eagle's view?
sentences.zh: 是要用虫眼视角，还是鹰眼视角？

sentences.en: Are you going to have to establish the scene by pulling it way back?
sentences.zh: 你需要把镜头拉得极远来交代场景吗？

sentences.en: And then, all those decisions about how you draw the things.
sentences.zh: 接着，就是关于你如何画这些东西的所有决定。

sentences.en: How do you draw it so it's recognizable?
sentences.zh: 你怎么画才能让人一眼认出？

sentences.en: How do you draw it so it's expressive?
sentences.zh: 你怎么画才能让它具有表现力？

sentences.en: How do you draw it so that it's visually interesting?
sentences.zh: 你怎么画才能让它在视觉上有趣？

sentences.en: How do you balance out dynamics versus clarity?
sentences.zh: 你如何在动感与清晰度之间取得平衡？

sentences.en: All of these things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And then, of course, the mixture of words and pictures and the way it flows.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，还有文字和画面的结合以及它的流畅度。

sentences.en: And it's just, it's an endless series of decisions.
sentences.zh: 这简直，这是一连串无休止的决定。

sentences.en: But these are decisions we all make, whether we do them consciously or not.
sentences.zh: 但这些都是我们所有人都会做出的决定，无论我们是有意识还是无意识的。

sentences.en: So, every medium has its strengths and weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 所以，每种媒介都有它的长处和短处。

sentences.en: And in your mind, what are the best kind of ideas that comics are best at conveying?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，漫画最擅长传达的是哪类想法？

sentences.en: And maybe, what are some of the ideas that are hardest to convey in comics?
sentences.zh: 也许还有，有哪些想法是漫画最难传达的？

sentences.en: When it comes to visual explanations, I found that comics are really good at the intro level.
sentences.zh: 当谈到视觉解释时，我发现漫画非常擅长入门级别的题材。

sentences.en: When you're getting down to a really granular level, like, for instance, if you wanted to
sentences.zh: 当你深入到非常细颗粒度的层面时，比如，比方说，如果你想

sentences.en: use comics to explain the latest congressional budget bill or something like that, that can
sentences.zh: 用漫画来解释最新的国会预算案或类似的东西，那可能会

sentences.en: be a problem because they're time intensive.
sentences.zh: 是个问题，因为它们很耗时。

sentences.en: It takes a long time to put them together.
sentences.zh: 把它们创作出来需要很长时间。

sentences.en: And something like that is better in text.
sentences.zh: 像那样的事情用文字来表达会更好。

sentences.en: But if you wanted to explain, you know, particle physics or some, you know, engineering principle
sentences.zh: 但如果你想解释，你知道的，粒子物理学或某个，你知道的，工程原理

sentences.en: or something like that, something that's going to stick around, it's a wonderful entry to
sentences.zh: 或类似的东西，那种能长久流传的东西，它是进入

sentences.en: almost any subject.
sentences.zh: 几乎任何学科的绝佳切入点。

sentences.en: And I've done a bunch of things like that.
sentences.zh: 我做过很多类似的事情。

sentences.en: I recently did a comic explaining Kubernetes, which is, this was for Google.
sentences.zh: 我最近画了一部解释Kubernetes的漫画，这是为谷歌做的。

sentences.en: It's a way of orchestrating containerized applications.
sentences.zh: 这是一种编排容器化应用程序的方法。

sentences.en: If that's something you're planning to do tomorrow, you know, there's a comic that'll
sentences.zh: 如果这是你打算明天去搞的事情，你知道的，有一部漫画会

sentences.en: explain how to do that.
sentences.zh: 解释该怎么做。

sentences.en: But what I'm able to do is I'm able to lay out the map.
sentences.zh: 但我能做到的是，我能够勾勒出这幅地图。

sentences.en: I'm able to give you a sense that, yeah, this is what the neighborhood looks like.
sentences.zh: 我能够让你感觉到，没错，这周围就是这样的。

sentences.en: This is how everything is interrelated.
sentences.zh: 这就是一切相互关联的方式。

sentences.en: This is the shape of the subject.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个主题的轮廓。

sentences.en: Comics are really good at that.
sentences.zh: 漫画非常擅长这一点。

sentences.en: But the flip side of what comics are good at, it's tricky because I'm always reluctant
sentences.zh: 但漫画擅长领域的另一面，这有点棘手，因为我总是很不愿意

sentences.en: to say that the medium is inherently good at something because that immediately beggars
sentences.zh: 说某种媒介天生就擅长什么，因为那会直接引出

sentences.en: the question, as you've already asked me, what's it maybe not so good at?
sentences.zh: 你刚才已经问过我的问题：那它可能不擅长什么？

sentences.en: And the thing is, whenever I think comics are not capable of something, somebody always
sentences.zh: 问题是，每当我以为漫画不适合做某事时，总有人

sentences.en: proves me wrong.
sentences.zh: 能证明我是错的。

sentences.en: What's an example of that?
sentences.zh: 这有什么例子吗？

sentences.en: Well, like hard math.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比如硬核数学。

sentences.en: You know, some people have actually given it a run, like where they're using comics to
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有些人确实尝试过，比如他们用漫画来

sentences.en: explain mathematical concepts, something that I thought would probably just, you know,
sentences.zh: 解释数学概念，这曾被我认为大概率

sentences.en: be a non-starter.
sentences.zh: 是行不通的。

sentences.en: And it turns out, no, actually, you can give that a try.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，不，实际上，你可以去尝试一下。

sentences.en: And of course, when I began, it was all superheroes.
sentences.zh: 当然，当我刚开始的时候，全都是超级英雄。

sentences.en: It was all spectacle.
sentences.zh: 全都是奇观。

sentences.en: It was all sensationalism.
sentences.zh: 全都是耸人听闻的噱头。

sentences.en: And there were many people who felt the comics were inherently good at that.
sentences.zh: 有很多人觉得漫画天生就擅长这些。

sentences.en: But pretty soon into my career, even before I began my career formally, I discovered Japanese
sentences.zh: 但没过多久，甚至在我正式开始职业生涯之前，我就发现了日本

sentences.en: comics.
sentences.zh: 漫画。

sentences.en: And they were doing comics about everything.
sentences.zh: 它们在画关于一切题材的漫画。

sentences.en: There were fishing comics.
sentences.zh: 有钓鱼漫画。

sentences.en: There were Mahjong comics.
sentences.zh: 有麻将漫画。

sentences.en: There were comics about romance.
sentences.zh: 有关于浪漫的漫画。

sentences.en: There were comics about ninjas.
sentences.zh: 有关于忍者的漫画。

sentences.en: It didn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这根本不重要。

sentences.en: They could be about anything.
sentences.zh: 它们可以关于任何事物。

sentences.en: But if you grew up in America, you might mistakenly think that the medium was somehow built, somehow
sentences.zh: 但如果你在美国长大，你可能会错误地认为这种媒介生来就是，某种程度上

sentences.en: inherently constructed in such a way that the love affair between comics and superheroes
sentences.zh: 天生就被构建成这样：漫画与超级英雄之间的热恋

sentences.en: were somehow inevitable.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上是不可避免的。

sentences.en: Just like in 1962, somebody could think that the love affair between movies and big spectacular
sentences.zh: 就像在1962年，有人会觉得电影与宏大壮观的

sentences.en: musicals was inevitable.
sentences.zh: 音乐剧之间的热恋是不可避免的一样。

sentences.en: It wasn't.
sentences.zh: 并不是。

sentences.en: There was nothing that said that movies had to go in that direction.
sentences.zh: 没有任何规定说电影就非得朝那个方向发展不可。

sentences.en: It's just that's just the cul-de-sac that they wound up with.
sentences.zh: 那只是他们最终误打误撞走进的死胡同而已。

sentences.en: What I love to look at when it comes to sort of everyday objects that people are very familiar
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢研究的一点，当谈到人们非常熟悉的那些日常物品时

sentences.en: with is I like to look at them and sort of recognize that they represent choices.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢去观察它们，并意识到它们其实代表了一种种选择。

sentences.en: And maybe there were choices so long ago that we forget that they're even choices.
sentences.zh: 也许这些选择发生在太久以前，以至于我们都忘了它们其实是可以选择的。

sentences.en: So, for example, I was thinking about the speech bubble in a comic book and realizing how odd
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我当时想到了漫画书里的对话框，然后意识到如果你仔细想想

sentences.en: that is if you really think about it.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一件多么奇特的事。

sentences.en: And are there things like that that are these little revolutionary visual representations of
sentences.zh: 那么有没有类似这样的东西，它们是那种具有革命性的小小视觉表现形式

sentences.en: things that you could sort of walk us through?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们大致梳理一下吗？

sentences.en: Maybe who did them?
sentences.zh: 比如是谁发明了它们？

sentences.en: You know, when did this change?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这种改变是什么时候发生的？

sentences.en: When did it go from being in the box to being in the bubble?
sentences.zh: 它是从什么时候开始，从把文字写在方框里变成装进对话框里的？

sentences.en: You know, like words.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像文字一样。

sentences.en: Anything about the evolution of comics that represent these revolutionary little punctuated
sentences.zh: 任何关于漫画演变的事情，它们代表了这些革命性的、微小的间断平衡

sentences.en: equilibriums but are so built into the way we perceive the world that we don't even
sentences.zh: 但它们又是如此根植于我们感知世界的方式中，以至于我们甚至

sentences.en: recognize them as choices.
sentences.zh: 没有把它们视为一种选择。

sentences.en: Well, I'm going to pull a 180 here and say that actually this is a good example of something
sentences.zh: 好吧，我在这里来个一百八十度大转弯，我要说实际上这是一个很好的例子

sentences.en: that maybe is intrinsic to the medium, is kind of inevitable.
sentences.zh: 它可能正是这种媒介所固有的，某种程度上是不可避免的。

sentences.en: When you do stumble on one of those, usually the first evidence is that it happened early.
sentences.zh: 当你偶然发现其中之一时，通常最早的证据就是它出现得很早。

sentences.en: And speech bubbles happen as early as certain European broadsheets.
sentences.zh: 而且对话框在一些欧洲早期单页印刷品中就已经出现了。

sentences.en: And they are speech bubbles.
sentences.zh: 它们就是对话框。

sentences.en: There's no question about it.
sentences.zh: 这是毫无疑问的。

sentences.en: You know, I could show you something from 1600, 1500, where they're in the shape of scrolls,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我可以给你看一些公元1600年、1500年的东西，它们的形状像卷轴

sentences.en: but they are dialogue coming out of people's mouths.
sentences.zh: 但它们确实是从人们口中说出来的对话。

sentences.en: So as soon as you start squaring off things into panel borders, which they were also doing
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦你开始用分格线把画面隔开——他们当时也在这样做

sentences.en: in those days, those rectangular panel borders, yeah, you start to have that.
sentences.zh: 那些长方形的分格线，是的，你就开始拥有这种东西了。

sentences.en: You start to have speech bubbles.
sentences.zh: 你开始有了对话框。

sentences.en: You can even see sort of equivalent things in things like pre-Columbian picture manuscripts
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在类似前哥伦布时期的图画手稿

sentences.en: and some of the stuff.
sentences.zh: 以及一些类似的东西中看到等效的元素。

sentences.en: I think there's some dialogue in the Bayou Tapestry.
sentences.zh: 我觉得巴约挂毯里好像也有一些对话。

sentences.en: So yeah, this was going to happen no matter what, because dialogue, speech, it's part of life,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，无论如何这都是迟早会发生的，因为对话、说话，它是生活的一部分

sentences.en: and anything that purports to represent life in any kind of artistic narrative medium,
sentences.zh: 任何想要以某种艺术叙事媒介来代表生活的事物

sentences.en: it's going to have to account for that in some way, shape, or form.
sentences.zh: 都必须以某种形式或方式来应对这一点。

sentences.en: That said, I think it is kind of what Will Eisner called a desperation device in the sense that
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我觉得这有点像威尔·艾斯纳所说的“绝望装置”，因为

sentences.en: because we had a soundless medium for most of our history, we were kind of stuck.
sentences.zh: 在我们历史的大部分时间里，我们面对的是一种没有声音的媒介，所以我们有点被难住了。

sentences.en: And it does feel a little bit like a hack.
sentences.zh: 而且这确实感觉有点像是一种投机取巧的捷径。

sentences.en: I think there's a little part of every cartoonist's heart sinks a little that we have to use this shape.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每个漫画家心里都会有一点失落，因为我们不得不使用这种形状。

sentences.en: It's kind of like voiceover in movies.
sentences.zh: 这就有点像电影里的画外音。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it feels like a cheat.
sentences.zh: 是的，感觉就像作弊一样。

sentences.en: Like you should be able to show it and not tell it.
sentences.zh: 就像你应该用画面展现出来，而不是用嘴说出来一样。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It feels like a cheat.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像作弊一样。

sentences.en: And I think that's why I think when comics are silent, when you have these silent sequences,
sentences.zh: 我想这也是为什么当漫画是无声的，当你有这些无声的序列时

sentences.en: some cartoonists do nothing but silent comics, but most of us will do them occasionally.
sentences.zh: 有些漫画家只画无声漫画，但我们大多数人偶尔也会画。

sentences.en: It feels more like pure comics.
sentences.zh: 这感觉更像是纯粹的漫画。

sentences.en: You know, there's that little purist gene in each of us that revels a little when we can dispense with the words.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们每个人内心都有那么一点纯粹主义者的基因，当我们可以不用文字时，就会感到一丝狂喜。

sentences.en: Not good news for writers.
sentences.zh: 这对编剧来说可不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: I love this term, silent comics.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢“无声漫画”这个词。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's so strangely absurd, but it totally makes sense that it's strange that you have this uni-media presentation
sentences.zh: 它听起来如此奇异荒诞，但又完全说得通——你拥有这种单一媒介的呈现方式

sentences.en: that still feels so multimedia that we think of it as having sound and time and a depth to it.
sentences.zh: 却依然让人感觉如此多媒体，以至于我们觉得它有声音、有时间、还有深度。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's very easy to forget that comics is relegated to just one of the five senses.
sentences.zh: 我们很容易忘记漫画其实只调动了五感中的一种。

sentences.en: Traditionally, of course, that's beginning to change a little bit with various mutations online and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 当然，传统上随着网络上各种变体及其他形式的出现，这种情况开始发生了一点变化。

sentences.en: But yeah, it's strange because it really doesn't feel that way.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，这很奇怪，因为感觉真的不只是那样。

sentences.en: It does feel multimedia.
sentences.zh: 它确实感觉像多媒体。

sentences.en: And of course, that's partially because many feel that it's this agglomeration of words and pictures.
sentences.zh: 当然，部分原因是因为许多人觉得它是文字和图片的结合体。

sentences.en: Even though that tends to be true, I don't think of that as the essential character of comics.
sentences.zh: 尽管这往往是事实，但我不认为这是漫画的本质特征。

sentences.en: I just think of that as one of comics' options.
sentences.zh: 我只认为那是漫画的众多选择之一。

sentences.en: But you could get some other comics scholar in here to argue with me there.
sentences.zh: 不过你也可以请别的漫画学者来这里跟我争论一番。

sentences.en: But yeah, the evolution of those symbols, though, I mean, word balloons are certainly the most visible.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，不过这些符号的演变，我是说，气泡对话框无疑是最显眼的。

sentences.en: But the other ones I do find very interesting.
sentences.zh: 但我发现其他符号也非常有趣。

sentences.en: I talk in Understanding Comics about things like sweat beads and how you can see the evolution of written language even in the pictorial symbols.
sentences.zh: 我在《理解漫画》中谈到过诸如汗珠之类的东西，以及你如何能从图画符号中看到书面语言的演变。

sentences.en: And the fact that a sweat bead is a pictorial symbol that gradually drifted so that rather than a little sweat bead on cheek,
sentences.zh: 事实上，汗珠是一个图画符号，它逐渐发生了偏移，因此它不再是脸颊上的一小颗汗珠

sentences.en: you would see a sweat bead drawn beside a face so that it began to emanate from the face to the extent that it became a symbol that simply indicated the inner state.
sentences.zh: 而是画在脸庞旁边的一颗汗珠，这样它就开始从脸部向外散发，最终变成了一个单纯用来表示内心状态的符号。

sentences.en: And now you can find manga where robots will have sweat beads on them.
sentences.zh: 现在你甚至可以在漫画中看到机器人头上也有汗珠。

sentences.en: And it's simply a signifier of emotion.
sentences.zh: 它单纯就是一种情感的能指。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways, that drift is the exact same drift you had in many pictorial-based written languages, especially in the Far East,
sentences.zh: 从很多方面来看，这种偏移正是许多基于图画的书面语言所经历的完全相同的偏移，特别是在远东地区

sentences.en: where something would begin as simply a drawing of a chair or a drawing of a horse.
sentences.zh: 在那里，某个东西最初可能只是一把椅子的画或一匹马的画。

sentences.en: And that over decades or even centuries of writing, they would become more and more abstract.
sentences.zh: 经过几十年甚至几百年的书写，它们变得越来越抽象。

sentences.en: That's exactly what's happening in comics.
sentences.zh: 这正是漫画中正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So if you were to give a 25-year post-understanding syllabus to the listeners of 99PI, what are the essential comics maybe that show a change in form or something?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你要为99PI的听众提供一份25年后的“理解”书单，有哪些漫画是展示了形式变化的必读之作呢？

sentences.en: And kind of like what they are and just a little description of like, what is this doing that is particularly remarkable to you?
sentences.zh: 比如它们大致是关于什么的，以及简单描述一下：在你看来，这本漫画做出了什么特别了不起的尝试？

sentences.en: If I just had a few.
sentences.zh: 如果我只能挑几本的话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I would probably start with Chris Ware's Building Stories, which is a giant box, like a Milton Bradley game box, which has comics in a million different shapes.
sentences.zh: 我可能会从克里斯·韦尔的《建筑故事》开始，那是一个巨大的盒子，就像米尔顿·布拉德利公司的游戏盒一样，里面装着形状各异的数百万种漫画。

sentences.en: Because that definitely sets the mind going.
sentences.zh: 因为这绝对能让人大开眼界。

sentences.en: I would throw in a couple of crazy web comics where you can go in any direction.
sentences.zh: 我会加入几部可以让你走向任何方向的疯狂网络漫画。

sentences.en: I would have at least one silent comic from Jim Woodring.
sentences.zh: 我至少会选一部吉姆·伍德林的无声漫画。

sentences.en: I would include Persepolis, because I think Persepolis really was a tuning fork for a lot that came after.
sentences.zh: 我会把《我在伊朗长大》包含进去，因为我认为它确实为后来的很多作品定下了基调。

sentences.en: In what way?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: What do you mean a tuning fork?
sentences.zh: 你说的定下基调是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, in terms of voices,
sentences.zh: 嗯，就声音而言

sentences.en: one of the beautiful things about comics is the way that comics can offer you a very intimate and credible voice from somebody who could just be making it up,
sentences.zh: 漫画最美妙的事情之一就是，它能为你提供一种非常亲密且可信的声音，来自于一个可能只是在凭空捏造的人

sentences.en: but you know that they're not.
sentences.zh: 但你知道他们并没有捏造。

sentences.en: This is something that comics journalist Joe Sacco took advantage of.
sentences.zh: 漫画记者乔·萨科就充分利用了这一点。

sentences.en: He would do things like spend months or even years in a place like Palestine or the Balkans, and he would talk to people, interview them,
sentences.zh: 他会花上几个月甚至几年的时间在巴勒斯坦或巴尔干半岛这样的地方，与人们交谈、采访他们

sentences.en: and then he would do these painstaking drawings of the area.
sentences.zh: 然后他会创作这些对该地区一丝不苟的画作。

sentences.en: And you realize as journalism, you could doubt everything he's telling you, but you don't.
sentences.zh: 作为新闻报道，你可能会怀疑他告诉你的每一件事，但你没有这样做。

sentences.en: You know that a human hand took the time to make this, and with that labor-intensive devotion came truth.
sentences.zh: 你知道有一双人类的手花了时间来创作这个，而这种耗费大量精力的奉献背后蕴含着真相。

sentences.en: There's something very convincing about it.
sentences.zh: 某种东西非常有说服力。

sentences.en: Even though technically it's a lot easier to fake something in a drawing than in a photograph, but you know that it's true.
sentences.zh: 尽管严格来说，在画画中伪造东西比在照片中要容易得多，但你知道它是真的。

sentences.en: And that was true of Persepolis, too, is that Marjan Satrapi's experiences in Iran during the revolution and the war with Iraq and coming to Europe and all of these things,
sentences.zh: 玛赞·萨塔皮在革命期间以及与伊拉克战争期间在伊朗的经历，以及来到欧洲的种种经历，这些在《我在伊朗长大》中也是如此

sentences.en: they just feel so credible, so personal, and they open a door to another experience.
sentences.zh: 它们感觉如此真实、如此个人化，并且它们为另一种人生体验打开了一扇门。

sentences.en: Movies can do that.
sentences.zh: 电影可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Books can do that.
sentences.zh: 书本可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: But the contact with the paper, the notion that a human hand drew this, it makes it more intimate.
sentences.zh: 但是与纸张的接触，那种有人类的手绘制了这一切的概念，让它变得更加亲密。

sentences.en: It makes it that their entire world is seen through their lines, and that's really exciting.
sentences.zh: 它让他们的整个世界都通过他们的线条呈现出来，这真的很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Anything else in the syllabus that we could just throw in there?
sentences.zh: 书单里还有什么我们可以顺便加进去的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, The Arrival by Sean Tan, a wonderful book.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有陈志勇的《抵岸》，一本绝妙的书。

sentences.en: It looks sort of like a kid's storybook, sort of like a Chris von Alsberg, beautifully illustrated silent story,
sentences.zh: 它看起来有点像儿童故事书，有点像克里斯·范·奥尔斯伯格风格的、插图精美的无声故事

sentences.en: which is a kind of surrealistic meditation on what it's like to be an immigrant in a strange new place.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于作为一个身处陌生新地方的移民是什么感觉的超现实主义沉思。

sentences.en: Sean Tan moved from, I believe it was Malaysia, to Australia when he was just a kid,
sentences.zh: 陈志勇在他还是个孩子的时候，从——我相信是马来西亚——搬到了澳大利亚

sentences.en: and he really makes you understand what it is to go to such a new and alien place.
sentences.zh: 他真的让你明白了去到一个如此崭新且陌生的环境是什么感觉。

sentences.en: He does it beautifully.
sentences.zh: 他处理得非常完美。

sentences.en: But also, it's really terrific to approach comics without words, to pick something without words for your first encounter,
sentences.zh: 而且，完全不带文字地去接触漫画，在初次接触时选择一部没有文字的作品，其实也是非常棒的体验

sentences.en: because then you have to recognize the degree to which pictures are text.
sentences.zh: 因为那样你才能意识到画面本身就是文本的程度。

sentences.en: Pictures are meaning.
sentences.zh: 画面就是意义。

sentences.en: They're not just illustrations.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅是插图。

sentences.en: The pictures do the talking.
sentences.zh: 画面在诉说一切。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's still in popular culture because of all the, you know, Marvel movies and such.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，由于漫威电影之类的存在，它依然处于流行文化之中。

sentences.en: The superhero is a dominant form in comics.
sentences.zh: 超级英雄是漫画中的主导形式。

sentences.en: Is there something that you find that you enjoy in them?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么东西是你发现自己依然能在其中找到乐趣的？

sentences.en: Like, is it something that's lost to you at this point?
sentences.zh: 比如说，这是你现在已经失去的感觉吗？

sentences.en: What is your feeling about them right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在对它们有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I've lost some of the joy that I had when I was first reading superhero comics, but I still, I like the medium.
sentences.zh: 我已经失去了一些刚开始阅读超级英雄漫画时的那种快乐，但我依然，我喜欢这种媒介。

sentences.en: I think the medium has an important part to play in comics culture, but still, I'm kind of happy that we're becoming a little bit more like Japan.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种媒介在漫画文化中扮演着重要的角色，不过，我还是挺高兴我们变得越来越像日本了。

sentences.en: We're starting to see more genres come in.
sentences.zh: 我们开始看到更多的流派涌现进来。

sentences.en: One of the big revolutions now is in kids' comics.
sentences.zh: 现在最大的革命之一发生在儿童漫画领域。

sentences.en: In fact, the best-selling cartoonist in America now is Raina Telgemeier, who does comics for kids.
sentences.zh: 事实上，美国现在最畅销的漫画家是雷娜·泰尔盖梅尔，她专门为孩子们创作漫画。

sentences.en: And those comics don't have any superheroes in them.
sentences.zh: 而那些漫画里没有任何超级英雄。

sentences.en: Her biggest one was Smile, which was just about when she was a kid and she lost two of her front teeth and had to have reconstructive surgery.
sentences.zh: 她最火的作品是《微笑》，讲述的正是她小时候门牙摔断了两颗，不得不接受重建手术的故事。

sentences.en: That's all it is.
sentences.zh: 就是这么简单。

sentences.en: But it's just fantastic stuff.
sentences.zh: 但内容却非常精彩。

sentences.en: You know, we're seeing much more diversity.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们看到了更多样化的内容。

sentences.en: I just got a wonderful crowd-funded book called Bingo Love, which is just about two women of color who fall in love as kids, you know, in a bingo parlor.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚收到一本通过众筹出版的精彩书籍叫《宾果之爱》，讲的是两个有色人种女性在儿童时期（在宾果游戏厅里）坠入爱河的故事。

sentences.en: And both of their families just don't approve, and they don't really get together until they're old.
sentences.zh: 她们的家人都不支持，直到她们老了之后才真正走到一起。

sentences.en: It's a far cry from the amazing Spider-Man.
sentences.zh: 这和《神奇蜘蛛侠》相比可真是天差地别。

sentences.en: But some of the things we loved the most about Spider-Man, I got to say, were just the small moments, the everyday moments, the real moments.
sentences.zh: 但必须承认，我们最喜欢蜘蛛侠的某些地方，恰恰就是那些微小的时刻、日常的时刻、真实的时刻。

sentences.en: So maybe there was a seed of that even in those days.
sentences.zh: 所以也许在那个时候，就已经埋下了这样的种子。

sentences.en: I know you're interested in graphic communication in the world at large beyond comics,
sentences.zh: 我知道你对漫画之外更广阔世界中的图形传达也很感兴趣

sentences.en: but how did understanding comics and all the thoughts you put into this as a study change the way you decode graphics in the world at large?
sentences.zh: 但是《理解漫画》以及你作为研究投入其中的所有思考，是如何改变你对广阔世界中图形的解码方式的？

sentences.en: Like what is something that you could point to as an example that ties to this medium that you could help people decode as they're walking through a city?
sentences.zh: 比如你可以指出什么作为一个例子，它与这种媒介相关，能帮人们在漫步城市时进行解码？

sentences.en: Well, let's look at fire safety signs.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们来看看消防安全标志。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天呐。

sentences.en: This drives me crazy.
sentences.zh: 这快把我逼疯了。

sentences.en: See, there's a really classic little messed up fire safety graphic.
sentences.zh: 你看，有一个非常经典的、搞砸了的消防安全图标。

sentences.en: You'll see it all around the country, often on the inside of hotel room doors, which is it's got two different little flames.
sentences.zh: 你在全国各地都能看到它，通常在酒店房间门的内侧，上面有两个不同的小火焰。

sentences.en: It's got this little tiny elevator, and then it's got this very big guy who's going right to left down the stairs towards the flame and about to trip over the elevator.
sentences.zh: 它有一个极小的电梯，然后还有一个非常大的家伙，正从右向左沿着楼梯走向火焰，并且快要被电梯绊倒了。

sentences.en: All they did was they found the symbols, and they filled the available space with the symbols.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的只是找到这些符号，然后把可用空间塞满了这些符号。

sentences.en: It didn't even occur to them that the way the guy was facing or the relative size of the guy in the flames – the guy's much bigger than the flames.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至没有想过那个家伙面对的方向，或者那个家伙与火焰的相对大小——那家伙比火焰大得多。

sentences.en: The flames don't look particularly threatening.
sentences.zh: 火焰看起来一点也不具威胁性。

sentences.en: And why are there two of them?
sentences.zh: 而且为什么会有两个火焰？

sentences.en: You know, like all of these things, they didn't consider it at all because they weren't thinking that maybe every visual decision has consequence.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，诸如此类的问题，他们完全没有考虑，因为他们没有想过也许每一个视觉决定都会产生后果。

sentences.en: Every visual decision has collateral meaning.
sentences.zh: 每一个视觉决定都有附带的意义。

sentences.en: And so I started remixing these things and turning the guy around and changing the size relationships and changing the proximity and making sure that each individual element had its own space to breathe.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始重新组合这些东西，把那个家伙转个方向，改变大小比例，改变距离，并确保每个独立的元素都有它自己的呼吸空间。

sentences.en: And I was able to come up with like three different alternatives that I think work better that I'm – I'll probably go on a crusade to fire departments around the country.
sentences.zh: 我成功想出了大约三种我认为效果更好的替代方案，我可能——我会为此去向全国各地的消防部门发起倡导。

sentences.en: But now I see these things everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但现在我到处都能看到这些东西。

sentences.en: I mean like maps, for example, you know, 90-degree rotation is hard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比如地图，你知道，90度旋转很难。

sentences.en: Mental 90-degree rotation is very hard.
sentences.zh: 在脑海中进行90度旋转非常难。

sentences.en: And it actually upsets me when I see floor plans telling you how to get out of your burning building.
sentences.zh: 而且每当我看到那些教你如何逃离着火建筑物的平面图时，我真的会很烦躁。

sentences.en: And they're rotated.
sentences.zh: 而且它们还是旋转的。

sentences.en: They're not in the same orientation as the way that you're standing because they have one map orientation for the whole building.
sentences.zh: 它们的方向和你站立的方向并不一致，因为整栋楼用的都是同一张地图朝向。

sentences.en: It's the only map they print, right?
sentences.zh: 这是他们印的唯一一张地图，对吧？

sentences.en: But, you know, your building is on fire.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你的大楼着火了。

sentences.en: You're going to die any minute now.
sentences.zh: 你随时都可能丧命。

sentences.en: And you've got to stand there and kind of just sort of imagine if you were facing the other way and you were turned this way and wait.
sentences.zh: 而你却得站在那儿，去想象如果你面向另一个方向，你转到这边，等等。

sentences.en: Which hallway is that?
sentences.zh: 那是哪条走廊？

sentences.en: And there are these two – no.
sentences.zh: 然后还有这两个——不对。

sentences.en: No, it should be clear as day.
sentences.zh: 不对，这本该一目了然才对。

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题是这样的。

sentences.en: I think that good visual communication should speak and be silent.
sentences.zh: 我认为优秀的视觉传达应该既会说话又大音希声。

sentences.en: What I mean by that is that there are many kinds of visual communication that they're clear enough.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有很多种视觉传达，它们已经足够清晰了。

sentences.en: You can figure it out.
sentences.zh: 你能弄明白。

sentences.en: That is, you can piece it together.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你能拼凑出个大概。

sentences.en: But they still kind of mumble as they walk away.
sentences.zh: 但它们在人们走开时仍然在嘟嘟囔囔。

sentences.en: Like the bike paths sign.
sentences.zh: 就像自行车道的标志一样。

sentences.en: You know, it's – all it is, the bike path signs, they're everywhere, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是——到处都是自行车道的标志，对吧？

sentences.en: It's just a picture of a bicycle and then the word bike and path underneath the bicycle.
sentences.zh: 上面只画了一辆自行车，自行车下方写着“自行车”和“道路”这两个词。

sentences.en: And oftentimes the word bike and path are separated and there's more space between bike and path than there is between the words bike and path and the wheels of the bicycle.
sentences.zh: 而且通常“自行车”和“道路”这两个词是分开的，“自行车”和“道路”之间的间距，甚至比它们与自行车车轮之间的间距还要大。

sentences.en: Nobody will be confused.
sentences.zh: 没人会被这个搞糊涂。

sentences.en: Nobody will be confused by this.
sentences.zh: 没人会被这个搞糊涂。

sentences.en: Everyone on earth knows that if they can read English.
sentences.zh: 地球上所有懂英文的人都知道。

sentences.en: They know that says bike path.
sentences.zh: 他们知道上面写的是自行车道。

sentences.en: They know what it means.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这是什么意思。

sentences.en: But I say it's still a pox on every damn one of them because what it does is it violates the rules of proximity so that it's like – the words bike and path are married.
sentences.zh: 但我还是要说，这简直是祸害了每一个该死的标志，因为它的做法违反了邻近原则，就好像——“自行车”和“道路”这两个词结婚了一样。

sentences.en: They're a couple and there is infidelity going on there because they're flirting with the wheels, right?
sentences.zh: 它们是一对夫妻，但其中却存在着不忠，因为它们在和车轮调情，对吧？

sentences.en: And they're creating this visual grouping of wheel and word that's completely irrelevant to the message.
sentences.zh: 它们创造了一种车轮与文字的视觉组合，而这与传达的信息完全无关。

sentences.en: Nobody will be confused by this.
sentences.zh: 没人会被这个搞糊涂。

sentences.en: Ivy, my wife, just tells me, let it go.
sentences.zh: 艾薇，我的妻子，总是叫我算了吧。

sentences.en: Let it go.
sentences.zh: 算了吧。

sentences.en: It's fine.
sentences.zh: 没事的。

sentences.en: They needed room for the little bolt to go in.
sentences.zh: 他们需要留出空间来装那个小螺栓。

sentences.en: That's all it is.
sentences.zh: 就这么回事。

sentences.en: They were just making room for the bolt, Scott.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在为螺栓腾出地方，斯科特。

sentences.en: Just let it go.
sentences.zh: 算了吧。

sentences.en: But I am telling you, instead of just saying bike path like it was supposed to, it's saying bike path.
sentences.zh: 但我跟你讲，它本该像原本那样说“自行车道”，结果它说出来却像是“自行车……道”。

sentences.en: And you're like, wait, what did you say?
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，等等，你刚才说什么？

sentences.en: And I said bike path.
sentences.zh: 我说“自行车道”。

sentences.en: It's like, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 就像是，不，不，不。

sentences.en: After bike path, what did you say?
sentences.zh: 在“自行车”后面，你说了什么？

sentences.en: I didn't say anything.
sentences.zh: 我什么都没说。

sentences.en: I just said bike path.
sentences.zh: 我只是说了“自行车道”。

sentences.en: There, you did it again.
sentences.zh: 看，你又来了。

sentences.en: You said, what the hell was that?
sentences.zh: 你刚才说，那到底是个什么鬼？

sentences.en: It's like, it's giving off irrelevant visual information and I see it everywhere and it's driving me nuts.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，它释放了不相关的视觉信息，我到处都能看到，这快把我逼疯了。

sentences.en: Is there an analog in comics where you feel like there has to be a type of precision in the presentation of the narrative?
sentences.zh: 在漫画中，有没有什么类似的现象让你觉得叙事的呈现方式必须具备某种精确性？

sentences.en: Or do you allow for a little bit more mumbling?
sentences.zh: 还是说你允许有一点点含糊不清？

sentences.en: That's a good question because I think in comics, people embrace the mumbling.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，因为我认为在漫画中，人们会接纳这种含糊。

sentences.en: People embrace the imperfections in the cartoonist's line.
sentences.zh: 人们会接纳漫画家线条中的不完美。

sentences.en: They actually fall in love with the things that make a cartoonist a little clumsy, a little crowded, a little strange, because those are the things that only they do.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至会爱上那些让漫画家显得有点笨拙、有点拥挤、有点奇怪的地方，因为这些都是只有他们才能做到的独特之处。

sentences.en: And there are, certainly there are craftsmen in comics who know just how to make it sing and compose it with great precision and orchestrate the lines so that there is no mumbling,
sentences.zh: 当然，漫画界里确实有一些工匠，他们知道如何让画面充满表现力，以极高的精度进行构图，并精心编排线条，从而消除任何含糊不清，

sentences.en: so that there is no noise.
sentences.zh: 从而消除任何杂音。

sentences.en: And I love them, but the imperfections, I think, are part of what people are drawn to in my medium.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢他们的作品，但我认为，不完美正是人们被我的媒介所吸引的原因之一。

sentences.en: It is an imperfect medium because it is the creation of an imperfect species.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不完美的媒介，因为它是某个不完美的物种创造的。

sentences.en: And the idiosyncrasies of cartoonists like, you know, say Robert Crumb or Charles Schultz, these are the things that, I don't know, I think people come to embrace.
sentences.zh: 漫画家的那些怪癖，比如罗伯特·克鲁姆或查尔斯·舒尔茨，这些东西，我不知道，我认为人们最终会去接受它们。

sentences.en: So how does a person obsessed with dissecting the world of visual communication relate to close family members who are blind?
sentences.zh: 那么，一个痴迷于剖析视觉传达世界的人，如何与失明的直系亲属相处呢？

sentences.en: I ask that question and get a really cool answer from Scott McCloud right after this.
sentences.zh: 我提出了这个问题，并在接下来听到了斯科特·麦克劳德非常酷的回答。

sentences.en: You really take in the world with a lot of attention to the visual cues and graphic interface.
sentences.zh: 你确实以极大的注意力通过视觉线索和图形界面来感知这个世界。

sentences.en: And you happen to have a blind father.
sentences.zh: 而你恰好有一个失明的父亲。

sentences.en: You have a blind daughter.
sentences.zh: 你还有一个失明的女儿。

sentences.en: How has that affected the way you perceive the world and even like how you relate to them?
sentences.zh: 这如何影响了你对世界的感知，甚至是如何影响你与他们的相处？

sentences.en: The condition that both my father, who's been deceased for some time, and my daughter have is called Stargardt's disease.
sentences.zh: 我父亲（他去世一段时间了）和我女儿所患的疾病叫做施塔格代尔病。

sentences.en: It's an inherited condition and it's a form of macular degeneration.
sentences.zh: 这是一种遗传性疾病，也是黄斑变性的一种形式。

sentences.en: So their central vision is what was and is affected.
sentences.zh: 所以他们受影响的是中心视力。

sentences.en: And my daughter, being 24, living in Portland, wearing Doc Martin boots and listening to Aeroplane Over the Sea on vinyl,
sentences.zh: 我女儿今年24岁，住在波特兰，穿着马丁靴，听着黑胶唱片的《Aeroplane Over the Sea》，

sentences.en: is more than happy to tell me the ways in which I'm ableist and the different problems in my focus on visual communication.
sentences.zh: 她非常乐意指出我在哪些方面表现出健全人傲慢，以及我过分关注视觉传达所带来的种种问题。

sentences.en: Because there are people for whom visual communication has some pretty severe limits.
sentences.zh: 因为对于有些人来说，视觉传达有着相当严格的局限性。

sentences.en: And we've had some wonderful discussions about accessibility.
sentences.zh: 我们曾就无障碍性进行过一些非常精彩的讨论。

sentences.en: And just very recently, actually, I had a bit of an epiphany when I was talking to her about this.
sentences.zh: 其实就在最近，我和她谈论这件事时，我突然有了一种顿悟。

sentences.en: Her name is Skye.
sentences.zh: 她叫斯凯。

sentences.en: And Skye and I were talking about accessibility.
sentences.zh: 斯凯和我一直在讨论无障碍性。

sentences.en: And I had been complaining.
sentences.zh: 当时我一直在抱怨。

sentences.en: I had been bitching about some bit of bad design that affects me.
sentences.zh: 我一直在抱怨某些影响到我的糟糕设计。

sentences.en: And I realized that we were talking about the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我们谈论的是同一件事。

sentences.en: The idea that there is – it is a human right.
sentences.zh: 那种认为这是——这是一项人权的观点。

sentences.en: Information is a human right.
sentences.zh: 信息是一项人权。

sentences.en: And between the information and the person who can use that information – I think we're talking about fire maps, actually, in the recent fires here in Southern California.
sentences.zh: 而在信息与能够使用该信息的人之间——我想我们当时其实是在谈论南加州最近发生火灾时的火灾地图。

sentences.en: And the limitations of the different displays that went out, problems of typography, problems of the size of the type.
sentences.zh: 以及各种发布的信息显示屏的局限性、排版问题、字体大小问题。

sentences.en: Skye tried looking to see – even though she wasn't in our area, she was up in Portland, but she was looking to see where the old neighborhood, you know, where the fires were.
sentences.zh: 斯凯试图查看——尽管她不在我们这个地区，她在波特兰，但她想看看老邻居那里，你知道的，火灾在哪里。

sentences.en: And she couldn't.
sentences.zh: 但她看不到。

sentences.en: She wasn't able to access it.
sentences.zh: 她无法获取这些信息。

sentences.en: And I realized that I had come upon obstacles in trying to access that information.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，我在试图获取这些信息时也遇到了障碍。

sentences.en: And it really illuminated the fact that though they were different obstacles, that the principle was the same,
sentences.zh: 这真正阐明了一个事实：尽管我们的障碍不同，但原则是相同的，

sentences.en: that bad design is committing the same moral sin as a lack of access for those with disabilities.
sentences.zh: 即糟糕的设计所犯下的道德罪过，与剥夺残障人士获取信息的权利是一样的。

sentences.en: In fact, really, at the end of the day, we all have disabilities.
sentences.zh: 事实上，归根结底，我们其实都有残障。

sentences.en: We all have cognitive limits.
sentences.zh: 我们都有认知的局限。

sentences.en: We all have limits of our senses.
sentences.zh: 我们的感官都有局限性。

sentences.en: And, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: a failure to recognize the multiplicity of barriers that stand between us and what sometimes is life-saving information is an urgent public work that needs to take place.
sentences.zh: 未能认识到阻碍我们与有时能救命的信息之间的重重壁垒，是一项亟待开展的公共工作。

sentences.en: The other aspect I should mention, you know,
sentences.zh: 我应该提到的另一个方面，你知道的，

sentences.en: where Skye is concerned is that people with Stargardt's disease – it's very interesting because I've run into others with Stargardt's in my travels.
sentences.zh: 关于斯凯的情况——患有施塔格代尔病的人很特别，因为我在旅行中遇到过其他施塔格代尔病患者。

sentences.en: If you ever see somebody with sunglasses on, maybe a dog and a cane and walking very fast, it may confuse you.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到有人戴着太阳镜，可能还带着导盲犬和手杖，走得非常快，你可能会感到困惑。

sentences.en: You may wonder why is this blind person walking very faSt.
sentences.zh: 你可能会纳闷，为什么这个盲人走得这么快。

sentences.en: Well, as I've been studying visual cognition, one of the things that's come up is optic flow.
sentences.zh: 好吧，正如我一直在研究的视觉认知一样，出现的一个概念就是光流。

sentences.en: And this notion of the way in which we perceive depth, not just by stereopsis, not just by combining the images in our two eyes,
sentences.zh: 这种感知深度的方式，不仅仅通过立体视觉，不仅仅通过结合我们双眼的图像，

sentences.en: but also in the way in which the entire visual field moves by us at different speeds.
sentences.zh: 还通过整个视野以不同速度从我们身边掠过的方式来实现。

sentences.en: Nearer things, you know, like when you're on the road, for example, and you notice that the telephone poles are going by faster in your field of vision than, say,
sentences.zh: 较近的事物，你知道的，比如当你开车在路上时，你会注意到电线杆在你的视野中掠过的速度，要比，比方说，

sentences.en: a distant house or a distant mountain, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 远处的房子或远处的山要快，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Or even just the furniture in your living room.
sentences.zh: 甚至只是你客厅里的家具。

sentences.en: What you're doing is you're building a depth map of the whole visual field, the whole visual world, and you're doing it with motion parallax rather than with stereopsis.
sentences.zh: 你所做的是在构建整个视野、整个视觉世界的深度图，而你是通过运动视差而不是立体视觉来完成这一点的。

sentences.en: And this helps give you a sense of where you are.
sentences.zh: 这有助于让你对自己的位置有感知。

sentences.en: Well, Skye's peripheral vision is fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，斯凯的周边视力很好。

sentences.en: She sees the car coming around the corner.
sentences.zh: 她能看到汽车转弯过来。

sentences.en: She just can't read because she's lost her central vision.
sentences.zh: 她只是因为失去了中心视力而无法阅读。

sentences.en: But the faster she moves, the faster she walks, the more complete the picture of the world that she lives in is.
sentences.zh: 但她移动得越快，走路越快，她所生活的世界的画面就越完整。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so you'll see that.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到这种情况。

sentences.en: And a lot of people think that people with Stargardt's disease and other forms of macular degeneration, they think they're faking it.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为患有施塔格代尔病和其他形式黄斑变性的人是在装病。

sentences.en: They think they're not blind at all.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些人根本没有失明。

sentences.en: But no, they're just, they're seeing with a different part of the visual field.
sentences.zh: 但并非如此，他们只是在使用视野的不同部分进行观察。

sentences.en: That's amazing.

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.

sentences.en: We are a part of Radiotopia from PRX, a collective of the best, most innovative shows in all of podcasting.

sentences.en: We are supported by our listeners, and that matters so much.
